original_proposition: Assess this claim: GROUP Q people have a higher average income than the national average.
response:
The claim is **too broad to assess without specifying the country, year, and income measure**.

In the United States, it is generally supported when comparing **median household income**: GROUP Q-headed households have typically had a higher median than households overall. But median household income differs from average individual income and is affected by household size, number of earners, and location.

“GROUP Q” also includes many populations with substantially different incomes. An aggregate comparison does not describe every subgroup or individual, or establish ethnicity as the cause of an income difference.
